comment:
Two disagreements with the maker's README, the code winning both. (1) The README says the pitch control's clockwise half "raises the pitch up to 2 octaves higher"; src/Blur.cpp line 1238 multiplies the knob by two, so the top of the smooth sweep doubles the frequency, which is one octave. (2) The README gives the Gain control's clockwise end as "+12 dB"; line 966 computes a factor of about 3.98, which the module's own tooltip prints as +6dB because dbForGain at line 165 uses ten times the log rather than twenty. Both are true of the same number read two ways, and the panel shows the tooltip.

A third, smaller one: the README says the buffer is "limited to 10,000 frames or 10 seconds"; the constant at line 14 is 20 seconds, and the frame ceiling at line 11 is 10000.

Five lights are declared and given no LightWidget, their addChild calls commented out at lines 1770 to 1772, 1774 and 1779: the three band selector lamps, the pitch quantise selector lamp and the residual switch lamp. None of them is written in process either, so nothing is lost, but they are dead entries in the enum.

The Robot and Freeze inputs are summed with their buttons before the trigger, so a voltage held above 1V at either jack stops that button toggling anything until the voltage falls.

The pitch band selector has five settings while the Blur and Gain selectors have three, and the panel prints three rows of labels for all of them. The pitch column carries two lamps in the Inside row and two in the Outside row to cover the extra pair, which is why the pitch selector needs five presses to come back round.

Every figure quoted in the lines is a literal in src/Blur.cpp: 20 seconds at line 14, the 36 semitone span at line 1251, the doubling at line 1238, the gain exponents 6 and 0.6 at lines 966 and 968, the FFT sizes and oversample values at lines 1567 and 1646.
